有人嘲讽我卖在低位，说实话这类人我见多了，有时懒得理。但正好强调一下我的方法，我看基本面，看估值，有时会加入技术面，但优先级最低。做基本面时短期的价格走势我不一定考虑，但 $NKE因为基本面的离场我认为完全没毛病。

name: 投资TALK君
text:
$TLT，没经验的误碰，我也不一定对，思路分享。
----------------------------------------------------------
有个错配，通胀预期（BREAKEVEN）跟随油价下跌，而美联储货币政策根据核心PCE做判断，所以油价下跌让BE下跌，但真实利率因为通胀数据不好，导致市场定价鹰派美联储，加息次数增加，所以上涨，结果是10年期名义上涨，TLT下跌。

影响真实利率：
1. 美联储货币政策预期
2. 经济增速预期
3. 期限溢价（财政部供给，流动性，养老金需求，货币政策稳定性等等）

AI资本开支如果放缓
1. 经济增速放缓（大概率），衰退（中小概率）
a. 消费放缓（股市下跌，财富效应）
b. 投资放缓
2. 通胀
a. 股市下跌，短期财富管理通胀下跌，直接影响PCE
b. 存储价格放缓（甚至负增长），短中期通胀下跌
3. 11月初的QRA已经暗示下个季度可能调整久期供给
后视镜的通胀数据不好，市场定价美联储加息，真实利率上涨，美联储跟随，即使油价下跌让通胀预期下跌，不足以抵消加息预期
TLT（TMF）进场点，美联储最鹰派的时候（把加息预期打满，但实际明年可能降息），注意12月联储会议

name: Gary
text:
From an NVIDIA employee: 

“To the Board,

I have worked at NVIDIA for nearly 18 years, and I feel compelled to share something personal during this extraordinarily difficult moment.

I am not writing to comment on the circumstances or to presume anything about the process the Board must undertake. I simply hope you will consider the perspective of someone who has had the privilege of working closely with Jensen for almost two decades—and who has seen firsthand the kind of leader and human being he has been to so many employees.

I first worked with Jensen in 2009 after I joined the company, when we went through 37 versions of GeForce posters for Chinese retail, and later through countless gaming events and the early China and Asia GTCs. He could challenge me quite publicly at times, but I always valued his candor, his teaching, and especially the conversations we had after those events.

One conversation in particular has stayed with me for nearly 17 years.

It was during a post-management QBR dinner in Hong Kong early 2010, I asked Jensen about something I had heard from an older employee: that during the difficult layoffs of 2008, he had personally called engineers who were being laid off and later reached out to many of them individually.

He told me a story about an elderly man he once met in a small grocery shop in Hong Kong. The man had worked there his entire life. Jensen asked him why he had never looked for another job. The man answered, “Because my boss took care of me in the rainy days.”

Jensen told me that sentence stayed with him. When he told me the story his glasses were covered by mists from his wet eyes. He promised himself that he would never forget the people who had entrusted their lives and careers to him. No matter how much pressure he faced, employees were family, and he wanted to be the person who would take care of them in the rainy days.

He kept that promise.

Through COVID, the Russia-Ukraine war, and countless other uncertain moments, I repeatedly heard him reassure employees, in one form or another: “I got you.”

Throughout the years, he has also put in countless personal efforts to make us feel at home. He created the quarterly “Global Free Days” and launched policies to support employees building their families via IVF and adoption, with the program fully funded by the company. From sending a soft blue blanket to congratulate me on my son’s birth, to visiting a member of my team in the hospital during Computex, he did everything he could to ensure we always felt cared for and supported, no matter the circumstances.

Many of us privately called him “Daddy Huang”—not as a joke, but with genuine affection, gratitude and admiration.

That was Jensen’s magic.

He didn’t just build technology. He created policies that changed people’s lives, and a company culture that made us so passionate about NVIDIA.

Stand behind Jensen Huang is a family, thousands of employees whose lives he has touched, and generations of people who have benefited from his leadership and his humanity.

I am only one employee, and I do not pretend that my voice can change the outcome of anything. But after nearly 18 years here, I could not remain silent without sharing what I have personally witnessed.

Please remember the extraordinary amount of humanity, kindness and opportunity that Jensen and his family have seeded around the world.

Please remember the people whose lives he has changed—not just through NVIDIA’s technology, but through his personal decisions, his empathy, and the culture he created.

And please remember that many of us are incredibly proud of him.

Whatever difficult decisions lie ahead, I hope the Board will approach them with both the rigor required of its fiduciary responsibility and the humanity deserved by a person who has spent so much of his life taking care of others in their rainy days.

With deepest respect,

A grateful NVIDIA employee of nearly 18 years”

name: Lex Fridman
text:
NVIDIA letting Jensen go is a huge mistake, for America and for humanity. It's Apple firing Steve Jobs all over again, but much bigger, given the role of AI in defining the future of our world.

I've been keeping quiet on this out of respect for Jensen's family and team, who I've met and who are amazing humans, and because I personally hate infidelity. So my heart goes out to them in this difficult personal family moment.

But I can also say that Jensen is human, and makes mistakes like all of us do. Not that I matter at all, but I've known Jensen for a long time and have gotten the chance to spend a lot of time with him, behind the scenes, away from mics and cameras. I have seen him show kindness, humility, care to everyone around him, including strangers, including from the poorest most struggling parts of society, treating all the same with the same thoughtfulness and attention, because they are fellow humans and not because he has something to gain from them. That shows rare character, to maintain humility and humanity through all of it.

Another data point is what people who know him well have said privately to me about Jensen over the years. I've never had anyone tell me anything but how awesome he is or how much they love him. Probably over a thousand people at this point. This includes hundreds of engineers, CEOs, colleagues, friends, etc.

Also, since there was some spy talk. Jensen is as proud  an American as it gets. I'm in shock frankly at all of this, including the mass hysteria around it. I love America, and I think NVIDIA letting Jensen go is terrible for America.

I stand with Jensen.

Love you all ❤️
